title: Measles-Infected Visitor Spent 11 Hours at Universal Studios Hollywood, Triggering Health Alert
excerpt: Los Angeles County officials warn anyone who visited the theme park on July 26 may have been exposed as the U.S. records its highest measles count since 1991.
body:
• A Ventura County adult with measles spent 11 hours at Universal Studios Hollywood on July 26, from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m.
  • The U.S. has recorded 2,371 confirmed measles cases in 2026 as of late July, the highest annual total since 1991.
  • Health officials identified additional exposure sites in Oxnard and Ventura, including a movie theater and a Walgreens pharmacy.
  • Anyone exposed should monitor for symptoms through August 16 and confirm their MMR vaccination status.

A person infected with measles spent an entire day at Universal Studios Hollywood on July 26, prompting public health officials in Los Angeles and Ventura counties to issue exposure warnings for thousands of potential visitors.

The infected individual, an adult from Ventura County who had recently returned from international travel, visited the theme park from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. — an 11-hour window during which the highly contagious virus could have spread through the packed attraction.

A Spreading Web of Exposure Sites

The measles case, confirmed on August 4, marks Ventura County's first in nine years. Health officials have identified multiple exposure locations beyond Universal Studios.

The visitor also stopped at a Subway restaurant in Oxnard before entering the park, visited Hacienda Furniture and Mattress from July 27 to August 1, attended the Cinemark Century Riverpark theater in Oxnard on July 31, and visited a Walgreens and a Kaiser Permanente medical office in early August.

"Our team has mobilized quickly to help alert the community and try to contain the spread. Ventura County is well positioned to respond effectively with our experienced staff and strong vaccination rates."

— Dr. Uldine Castel, Ventura County Health Officer

Part of a National Surge

The exposure comes as measles continues a dramatic resurgence across the United States. The CDC has confirmed 2,371 cases in 2026 as of late July — the highest annual total since 1991. The increase is driven by declining vaccination rates in some communities and increased international travel during summer months.

"With summer travel underway, the risk of exposure to infectious diseases may increase," said Muntu Davis, the Los Angeles County public health officer. "We urge everyone to confirm their immunity and get the MMR vaccine if needed, especially before traveling and attending crowded events."

Measles is one of the most contagious viruses known. It spreads through the air when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes, and the virus can linger on surfaces and in the air for up to two hours after the person has left. About 90% of unvaccinated people exposed to measles will contract the disease.

What Visitors Should Do

Officials said anyone who was at Universal Studios Hollywood on July 26 during the exposure window could develop symptoms seven to 21 days after exposure. Visitors should monitor for symptoms through August 16.

Measles symptoms include high fever, cough, runny nose, and red, watery eyes, followed three to five days later by a rash that starts on the face and spreads across the body. Severe complications can include pneumonia, encephalitis, and in rare cases, death — particularly in young unvaccinated children and immunocompromised individuals.

Those who have received the recommended two doses of the MMR vaccine are likely protected but should still watch for symptoms. People who develop symptoms should stay home, avoid public places, and call a healthcare provider before visiting a medical facility.

Echoes of Past Theme Park Exposures

The incident recalls previous measles scares at Southern California attractions. In 2025, a teenager from New Zealand with measles visited Disneyland, Universal Studios, and LAX while infectious. A decade earlier, a major outbreak linked to Disneyland spread across California and multiple states.

People with questions about measles exposure in Ventura County can call the county's information line at 805-652-7599.
